newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kredietbank to stay independent, no partner needed.
newsitem.headline: Kredietbank to stay independent, no partner needed.

text.p: Belgian Kredietbank, one of the country's top four banks, said that it planned to stick to its long standing strategy of staying independent and saw no need for a partner.
It also denied market talk that it was in merger talks with French Credit Commercial de France, adding that both banks had been "good friends" for many years.

"We do not quite subscribe to the attitute that one has to be big to survive. Our way is to grow on our own. We have proven that this strategy is very successful. We see no reason at all why we would change this," Kredietbank chief executive officer Marcel Cockaerts said in reply to questions at a news conference about 1996 earnings.

Asked about the possibility that Kredietbank's two main rivals, Generale Bank and Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL) would merge, Cockaerts said: "We have no problem with a 'Big Belgian Bank'. We will be happy to be the 'Fast Other Bank'."
"I would not be concerned by a Big Belgian Bank. We are big enough to be considered worthwile partners by major corporate customers. We are players in the big events," Cockaerts said.

He added that if the two other banks did merge, this could have advantages for Kredietbank as many bank customers liked to have more than one bank, and some customers of the new entity might defect to Kredietbank.
Kredietbank director Remi Vermeiren told Reuters that he expected between five and 15 percent of the customers of a combined Generale-BBL bank could leave to join other banks.
Cockaerts said that Kredietbank's independent stance did not mean that it would refuse to consider any alliance offer.
"We are not stubborn. Our independent strategy does not mean that we do not keep our ears and eyes open," he said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
